definition: Arbiter means one who settles a dispute brought before them with a final, binding decision.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word arbiter. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know arbiter should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Both bands accepted the festival's stage manager as arbiter of set-length disputes, and her stopwatch ruling was final.
An adviser is the mildest voice here — advice can be thanked and ignored, while an arbiter's word ends the argument.
A moderator stops short of an arbiter: moderators keep the discussion orderly and fair but decide nothing, while the arbiter's decision binds both sides.

An umpire rules on play-by-play calls inside a game, applying a fixed rulebook in real time. An arbiter is chosen by the two sides themselves to settle their whole dispute, and the decision binds because both agreed in advance to accept it. Umpires enforce rules; an arbiter ends arguments.

A judge holds state office and presides in a courtroom, with authority that comes from the government, not from the people in the case. An arbiter can be anyone — an aunt, a stage manager — so long as both sides agree that this person's word will settle the matter.

An arbiter is stronger than an adviser and more final than a go-between: both sides agree beforehand that this one person's word will bind them.
That advance agreement — and the binding decision — are what the word names.
